w1_final.reason: Core facts are new production-level developments not covered by existing events: (1) VR300 final BOM raises HBM4E to 640GB, reversing E171's 512GB plan; (2) an incremental binding Micron purchase order for the 640GB config separate from the existing baseline; (3) increased HBM wafer-start and packaging allocation for VR300; (4) Micron 245TB QLC SSDs standardized as VR300 inference-cluster data tier with two purchase releases and per-cluster storage raised from 20.4PB to 27.2PB—beyond E80's general 'working with storage vendors' fact.

candidates.proposition: NVIDIA's final production bill of materials for the VR300 platform raised HBM4E capacity to 640GB per accelerator, replacing the 512GB level in the prior production plan.
An incremental binding purchase order for additional qualified HBM4E packages at the 640GB configuration was issued to Micron for VR300, separate from the existing HBM supply baseline.
Micron and the NVIDIA platform supply group raised the allocation of HBM wafer-start capacity and advanced-packaging slots assigned to the VR300 program beyond the prior plan.
NVIDIA's VR300 production architecture designated Micron 245TB QLC SSDs as the standard high-capacity data tier for inference clusters.
The VR300 cluster design increased deployed storage from 20.4PB to 27.2PB per standard inference cluster.
Two purchase releases for the 245TB QLC standard-cluster configuration were issued to Micron, establishing a repeat-purchasing pattern rather than a one-time sample or qualification-only lot.
